title: R49 东西六宫及同区厅殿名称匾实景审查
scope: 21 named halls in east-six/west-six, 20 registered nameboards; Yonghe photo adjudication is delegated to owner. Cining is in outer-west and is audited by a separate worker.
method: Read actual zone data and R49 registered-nameboard scan.
Build actual baseline Three.js CPU geometry, read nameboard/backing bounds and actual header bounds without GPU/browser.
Inspect downloaded official image pixels, including wide views and plaque close-ups.
Probe Chonghua and Yangxin baoxia at actual face depths with vertical CPU rays.
Do not treat 9/9 visibility as historical validation.
criticalFindings: Chonghua cannot fit a historically plausible plaque above its modeled door without resolving a low baoxia underside.
Fengxian real nameboard is between two eaves, but the current model has a single eave.
Generic domestic boards dip below the generated door header by approximately 0.34–0.38m including frames.
Lijingxuan and Tongdaotang model labels are not the literal historic plaques.

singleEaveMountingRule.photoSupportedPrinciple: Principal single-eave palace plaques occupy the front surface of the painted architrave/bracket band. Vertical overlap with those beam bands is normal; a beam-bottom height is NOT a universal upper limit.
singleEaveMountingRule.geometryRequirement: Keep the full backing above the door-header reference; keep backing behind the face but outside the front skin of beams and walls; inspect actual roof/rafter intersections separately.
singleEaveMountingRule.preferredCorrection: Translate upward and adjust depth per facade before shrinking. Retain existing scale if roof geometry and source proportions permit.
exceptions: Yonghe and Chonghua have baoxia overhead geometry requiring a separate fit.
Fengxian is an inter-eave plaque with missing model structure.
Lijingxuan is an attested horizontal plaque but current model label is vertical.

chonghuaRelativePixelCheck.interpretation: The front baoxia architrave/column head visibly stands higher than the rear hall door/transom, not approximately level with it. The existing column-top above-floor / door-height ratio is only 1.136. A hypothetical column-top 6.45m would give about 1.475, within the visual scale but NOT measured or validated.
chonghuaRelativePixelCheck.limitations: Points are approximate on a 1000px image. Foreground and background lie at different depths; ratios are NOT perspective-corrected. This cannot establish a literal 6.45m height. Roof connection to the main hall still needs engineering/visual verification.
chonghuaRelativePixelCheck.minimumSourceConsistentProposal: If building changes are authorized, prefer a coherent whole-baoxia raising with column feet retained and column/beam/roof relations maintained over an unsubstantiated rear-only sloping underside. Do not implement from this report alone; approval belongs to the owner.
